3.0.0.en: The Law states in (Deut 24:1-4) that if a man divorces his wife and she becomes another man's, he may not take her back as his wife afterwards. But God addresses Jerusalem, or His people the Jews, as a bride of His who left Him and attached herself to the worship of idols with many gods, that is, she committed spiritual adultery many times; and yet God shows His surpassing love in His readiness to receive her as His wife a second time if she repents and returns to Him. The love of God surpasses human feelings, which refuse to take back a woman who has lain with others.

3.1.0.en: God compares His people to the harlot who sits by the road waiting for her customers, or to the Arab who sits in the desert; that is, His people longed for the worship of idols and for clinging to evil lusts, and yet God is ready to receive them if they return to Him in repentance.

3.2.1.en: The latter rain: which falls at the end of the planting season, that is, in the months of March and April. A whore's forehead: the harlot used to put a mark on her forehead so that her customers could easily recognize her, so the forehead of the harlot signifies shamelessness.

3.2.2.en: Nature expressed its distress at the adultery of the people of God by the withholding of rain, and consequently the drying up of crops and the occurrence of hunger, so that perhaps the affliction would alert the people of God who persisted in adultery; but sadly they refused to obey the commandments of God and return to Him in repentance.

3.3.0.en: If Jerusalem repents, she remembers God's fatherhood and His care for her in the wilderness of Sinai, and calls Him the guide of her youth, when she enjoyed fellowship with Him and rejoiced in His care.

3.4.0.en: God is tender, even if He is angry with His people because of their many sins, and even if He allows them the affliction of captivity, it is a temporary affliction, because He returns and receives them and forgives them in spite of all the sins that they committed with insistence and stubbornness; He receives them if they return to Him.

3.4.1.en: If God is merciful and forgiving toward you whatever your sins may be, then be long-suffering also toward those around you whatever their sins may be. Be merciful and find excuses for others, so that you deserve the mercies of God.

3.5.s.en: (2) Judah's not returning in spite of the captivity of Israel

3.5.0.en: Israel: this includes the ten tribes and is called the northern kingdom, whose capital was Samaria. Jeroboam the son of Nebat divided it after the death of King Solomon, and two tribes remained, Judah and Benjamin, which formed the southern kingdom, called the kingdom of Judah, whose capital was Jerusalem, where the temple was, and Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned over it. The captivity of Israel took place at the hands of the Assyrians, and Judah remained in the days of Jeremiah, but it was taken captive afterwards by Babylon, also during the lifetime of Jeremiah.

3.5.1.en: The prophecy of Jeremiah began in the thirteenth year of King Josiah, which means that these words were the first of Jeremiah's prophecies that God instructed him in. God spoke to him about the corruption of the kingdom of Israel by its worship of idols on the mountains and also under the shade of trees, that is, it fell into the worship of many pagan gods.

3.6.0.en: In spite of all the evil that the kingdom of Israel did, God called it to repentance through many prophets, such as Isaiah, but it refused to return to Him; and Judah saw Israel's persistence in its disobedience and its rejection of the prophets, and did not take warning but imitated it.

3.7.0.en: The reasons: all the evils that Israel did.

3.7.1.en: A bill of divorce: God rejected her and left her to captivity so that she would be joined to foreign kings who would rule over her. God was long-suffering toward Israel so that she might repent, but she did not repent, so He had to allow her the affliction of captivity, hoping that she might repent. But the kingdom of Judah did not learn from God's punishment of Israel, but she too continued in her spiritual adultery, that is, the worship of idols.

3.8.0.en: The lightness of her whoredom: the humiliation and shame of her adultery.

3.8.1.en: Stones: the stone statues of the pagan gods.

3.8.2.en: Stocks: idols made of wood, or wooden pagan temples. Judah persisted in her evil and fell into the worship of what are not gods, that is, the stone and wooden idols, and left God, her true God.

3.9.0.en: Judah fell into another sin, which was her pretending to return to God by way of outward worship, so she was false in this return.

3.10.0.en: By the multitude of Judah's falls she became worse than Israel, who became more justified before God than Judah. For Judah's sin is that she did not learn from God's warning to her through the captivity of Israel, and then she persisted in the worship of idols and refused repentance, hiding behind superficial worship without spirit.

3.10.1.en: If God alerts you to return to Him in repentance, do not be lax, and do not think that the presence of some social virtues, or people's praise of you, or your attachment to the form of worship in the Church will defend you before God, for there is no way to obtain true righteousness except by repentance.

3.11.0.en: Toward the north: toward the kingdom of Israel, although it was taken captive to Assyria and only a few Jews remained in it, yet by the prophecy he calls all the captives.

3.11.1.en: Jeremiah now directs his prophecy to the northern kingdom of Israel, which was taken captive because of its evil, and in his prophecy he shows how Israel is to repent, which is summarized in the following:

3.11.2.en: 1- Returning to God, for there is no solution to all their problems except faith in God and life with Him.

3.11.3.en: 2- Trust in the mercy of God, for He is very compassionate, tender and forgiving.

3.12.0.en: You have scattered your ways to the strangers under every green tree: this means the worship of strange gods under the trees, where statues of idols were set up.

3.12.1.en: He continues to lay down steps of repentance:

3.12.2.en: 3- Examining the soul to know its iniquity and its sin.

3.12.3.en: 4- Obeying God, because sin is disobedience to Him.

3.12.4.en: 5- Every sin that a person commits toward others is directed against God, and he must repent of it before God: “You have sinned against the LORD your God.”

3.13.0.en: I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion: He gathers the people of Israel scattered in the Assyrian kingdom and brings them back from captivity to Jerusalem when they repent. He continues the steps of repentance, saying:

3.13.1.en: 6- Trust in the sonship of God, so I reject the sins that anger Him.

3.13.2.en: 7- God is the only King over the heart, and He solves all problems and brings Israel back from captivity, so it is necessary to return to Him in repentance for the solution of problems.

3.13.3.en: Look at the tenderness of God and His love that calls you to repentance, so that you are not distressed by the multitude of your sins; for even if you grow weary and hate yourself, God still loves you and is ready to restore to you your splendor and your joy.

3.14.0.en: According to mine heart: they agree with the will of God.

3.14.1.en: Knowledge and understanding: knowing the commandments of God and understanding them by His Holy Spirit.

3.14.2.en: God rejoices in the repentance of His people and gives them many blessings, which are:

3.14.3.en: 1- He gives them pastors, that is, priests and teachers submitted to Him, who speak His word and are faithful in their care of the people.

3.15.0.en: Neither shall it be done any more: they will no longer perform the worship, or the sacrifices and offerings that are offered in the temple of Solomon. He continues the blessings of repentance, saying:

3.15.1.en: 2- A prophecy about Christianity, when the believers in Christ multiply and no longer need a symbol of the presence of God, which is the Ark of the Covenant, but Jerusalem, that is, the Church of the New Testament, becomes the throne of the Lord and spreads in every place, so that the Gentiles believe in Christ and repent of their straying and their stubbornness in sin.

3.16.0.en: The land of the north: where they were captive in Babylon.

3.16.1.en: The land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers: the land of Canaan, that is, Jerusalem and Judea.

3.16.2.en: 3- The return from the captivity, which happened at the beginning of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, when the Jews return, whether from the kingdom of Judah or the kingdom of Israel, and worship the LORD in Jerusalem.

3.17.0.en: How shall I put thee: it expresses the greatness of the grace of sonship, whose beauty cannot be expressed.

3.17.1.en: Ye shall not turn away from me: steadfastness in eternal happiness and life with God.

3.17.2.en: 4- The grace of sonship that God gives to His bride, that is, His people, so that she calls Him her Father after He has brought her back from captivity and given her the desirable land of Canaan as an inheritance, which He took from the wicked nations that He drove out before her. The land of Canaan signifies the Church of the New Testament with all the desirable things of the work of the Holy Spirit in it, and it signifies even more the heavenly Jerusalem, in which are all the longings of the souls that loved Christ, and which enjoys the inheritance of the glory of glories that is given to the Gentiles who believed in Christ as an eternal inheritance.

3.17.3.en: Do not be deceived by the temporary pleasure of sin, for it passes away, but look at the unspeakable blessings that you feel in part in your life on earth and then in heaven, so that you turn to repentance and reject every evil however attached to it you may be.

3.18.0.en: Her husband: the husband to whom she was joined and united in marriage.

3.18.1.en: God rebukes His people the children of Israel because they fell into many sins, the most important of which are the worship of idols and adultery and all the sins connected with them. He declares clearly that sin is betrayal of God, since it is clinging to another god, namely the idols and the lusts; and He compares their betrayal to the betrayal of a married woman against her husband by clinging to another man.

3.19.0.en: The children of Israel plunged into the worship of idols and lusts on high places, such as hills, thinking that on them they draw near to the gods they worship. And on the same places the enemies attacked and seized them and took them captive, so they cried out with bitter weeping because of the evil, the shame and the weakness that came upon them. This is the natural result of sin and of persisting in it.

3.19.1.en: Do not persist in sin, but if you fall into it, return quickly to God, lest He abandon you and many afflictions come upon you, which He allows because of His love for you, so that you return to Him and find the salvation of your soul.

3.20.0.en: God intends by afflictions the return to Him of His disobedient children, for He is their Father even while they are in their sins and He seeks the salvation of their souls; and how great is His joy at their repentance and return to Him and their confession that He is their God, and not the strange gods and the evil lusts.

3.21.0.en: The hills, the multitude of mountains: all the pagan worships that they practiced on these high places in order to draw near to the pagan gods.

3.21.1.en: When the people return to God they declare the futility of everything they relied on, the strange gods and the evil lusts that they thought were wealth, and they declare that deliverance from every sin and toil, and the gaining of happiness, is from God alone.

3.22.0.en: Shame hath devoured: one of the effects of sin is that it makes a person lose everything he has, but when the people of God repented they remembered that sin is accompanied by shame and loss, as happened to their fathers when they sinned and lost their possessions of sheep and cattle, and even lost their sons and daughters. Sin is a temporary pleasure with which Satan entices us, but he is fierce, attacking us and devouring the dearest things we have, our children and our resources.

3.23.0.en: In repentance the people declare that they plunged and lay down in sin and were defiled by it like their fathers, and rejected their loving God and Savior, and this would have led to their eternal destruction, but now they return to God in repentance, so that they may obtain their salvation.

3.23.1.en: Remember your past and present sins so that they drive you to repent with humility, and you will obtain the mercies of God, for He is a tender Father who cannot reject you whatever your sins may be.

3.23.2.en: A call to repentance because of the coming ruin

4.0.1.en: Remove: go astray and depart from God.

4.0.2.en: God calls His people to repent of their sins, the first and most important of which is to remove the statues of the pagan gods and be rid of them, and so to turn back from the way of their error.

4.0.3.en: Let your repentance be practical, not only in words, but by cutting off the causes and sources of evil, whether places, or friends, or habits, or viewing, and by beginning spiritual practices, so that you enjoy true repentance and fellowship with God.

4.1.0.en: The second proof of repentance is not to resort to the pagan gods and trust in them by swearing by them, but to swear by the name of God, the only God on whom His people rely, and by this God blesses His people, and faith even spreads from the people of God to the Gentiles, so that they believe in God and are blessed in their lives, and He becomes their glory and their strength.

4.2.0.en: Break up: ploughing is an agricultural operation in which the earth is cut open with the blade of the plough and turned over, bringing out the roots of the thorns so that we are rid of them.

4.2.1.en: The Lord calls to His people in the kingdom of Judah, where His city Jerusalem and His holy temple are, to cleanse their hearts from sin. He compares the heart that is full of evil and then pretends to worship God to ground full of thorns in which good seed is then sown: if this seed sprouts, it will be mixed with thorns. So the ground must first be ploughed to pull out these thorns and be rid of them, and then good plants sown, that is, repentance from sins and purification of the heart, and then the beginning afterwards of holy worship and good works. Circumcise yourselves: this is the cutting of a part of the male reproductive organ, which God commanded Abraham as a sign of his faith and that of his descendants; it signifies the cutting off of evil and the beginning of a new life with God, which is accomplished in the sacrament of Baptism. Foreskins: uncircumcision.

4.2.2.en: God calls His people not to the physical circumcision but to the spiritual circumcision of hearts, that is, the cutting off of evil from the heart by repentance; and if He means the physical circumcision for those who neglected it, He also means that it should be accompanied by the purification of the heart from every evil as a proof of faith in God.

4.2.3.en: Then He threatens His people that if they neglect repentance and the purification of their hearts and persist in evil, they thereby provoke God, so He is angry with them and punishes them with a wrath like fire that consumes them, as the Scripture says, “Our God is a consuming fire” (Deut 4:24).

4.2.4.en: Do not keep any sin in your heart however small, and do not rely on your mastery of worship with its rites and hymns, your knowledge of the Holy Bible, and all the good works you do, for they will not profit you if you do not first repent.

4.3.0.en: God warns His people of the beginning of the divine wrath against them because of their persistence in evil, so He asks that the trumpet be blown so that the people take refuge in the fortified cities, because the enemies, that is, the Babylonians, will attack and destroy and take them captive.

4.3.1.en: The fortified cities signify the churches in which the believers of the New Testament take refuge by many prayers, to be delivered from the evils of the world and the wars of the devil.

4.4.0.en: He warns them by the raising of the standard of war against the Babylonian attack upon them from the north, and cautions them of a great destruction, that is, a crushing defeat that will come upon them.

4.5.0.en: He compares the Babylonian kingdom to a lion, violent in its attack, coming out of its thicket, that is, Babylon, which destroys cities and kills those in them, while the rest flee and their inhabitants abandon them.

4.5.1.en: And Babylon, or the lion, signifies Satan, as our teacher Peter says, “Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: whom resist stedfast in the faith” (1 Pet 5:8, 9).

4.6.0.en: Gird you: put on the girdle, which is what is worn on the waist and extends down toward the legs. Sackcloth: coarse garments.

4.6.1.en: He calls the people so that they may benefit from the affliction of captivity and return to God in repentance, wearing sackcloth as a girdle on their waists and weeping over their sins because of God's wrath against them; and then God receives them, lifts His wrath from them and brings them back from captivity.

4.7.0.en: From the distress of the enemy's attack, all those responsible for Judah lose their ability to act, whether the king, or the prince, or the priest, or the prophet, because they departed from God and His wrath came upon them.

4.8.0.en: The sword reacheth unto the soul: the killing of many of the people of God.

4.8.1.en: The people blame God because He deceived them through the prophets, saying that they would have peace, and then they were surprised by the Babylonians attacking them and killing them. These troubles had not yet happened, but Jeremiah prophesies that they will happen, because the people thought that the false prophets were prophets from God, and they deceived them by prophesying peace to them. This prophecy is a warning to the people of God against listening to the words of the false prophets, and a call to them to repent of their sins, because of which God will bring His wrath upon them and the Babylonian attack.

4.9.0.en: Fanning: an agricultural operation by which the grains of wheat are separated from the chaff, and the presence of wind helps to accomplish it.

4.9.1.en: He compares the Babylonian attack to a hot, that is, strong, wind, by which God does not mean to help in agricultural work such as fanning and cleaning the grain, but a violent wind, stronger than the one that helps agricultural operations, which will come from the bare heights, that is, from the high places in the north, that is, Babylon. By this wind or this attack God means to discipline His people and judge them, so that they review themselves and repent.

4.9.2.en: Do not listen to any teachings foreign to the Church, so that no one leads you astray, and pay attention to the guidance of your father of confession and to prayer, and God will keep you in all your ways and lead you in the way of His Kingdom.

4.10.0.en: God compares the Babylonian attack, in addition to the lion and the east wind (vv. 7, 8), to the following:

4.10.1.en: 1- Clouds: the enemy will be strong and high above the Jews, and it is not possible to rise to his strength or to repel him.

4.10.2.en: 2- His chariots shall be as a whirlwind: the enemy's war chariots will be strong as a whirlwind, sweeping and overwhelming the Jewish people before them.

4.10.3.en: 3- His horses are swifter than eagles: the enemy's horsemen riding on horses attack with lightning speed as eagles swoop on their prey, killing and capturing the Jews.

4.10.4.en: The cities of Judah will be destroyed because of the force of the Babylonian attack. All this is by God's permission to discipline His people so that they repent of their sins.

4.11.0.en: God calls His people in the kingdom of Judah, in the person of the capital Jerusalem, to wash their sins by repentance, that they may be saved from this discipline, because their evil is the cause of these afflictions. He regards all their worship of idols and their evils as vain and without profit, and indeed as the cause of all this punishment.

4.11.1.en: The only way out for you, and the first thing you do when you fall into an affliction, is to repent of your sins and ask in faith and humility that God lift it from you, so that you are washed in the sacrament of confession and partake of the Holy Mysteries, and are strengthened and your life is renewed.

4.12.0.en: Here he speaks of the affliction of the northern kingdom of Israel when the Assyrians attacked it, and mentions some of its regions, namely the city of Dan and its surroundings, then the tribe of Ephraim, which holds the largest area in the kingdom of Israel, and how they all felt the calamity that came upon them as a discipline from God.

4.13.0.en: The nations: the armies of Babylon.

4.13.2.en: Give out their voice against the cities of Judah: they occupy them and take control of them.

4.13.3.en: God commands the prophet to warn Jerusalem that the armies of Babylon, coming from afar, will attack her and besiege her and all the land of Judea and occupy it.

4.14.0.en: He declares the reason for the discipline of the kingdom of Judah, which is her disobedience and her rebellion against God by the multitude of her sins, so He allowed the Babylonians to besiege her like watchers who surround those they guard, but this guarding is against Judea and not a protection for them.

4.15.0.en: These: the afflictions that came upon Judea.

4.15.1.en: Here he affirms the bitterness of the sin that Jerusalem and Judea committed; it was not merely outward faults but came from the heart, so it caused all this distress and humiliation.

4.16.s.en: (5) The prophet's grief for his people

4.16.0.en: Here appear the tender feelings of Jeremiah, who suffers greatly because of the ruin coming upon the kingdom of Judah on account of her sins, and the war and the sound of its trumpet announcing the Babylonian attack, and it appears that his grief is very deep in his bowels and his heart.

4.16.1.en: May you, as a father, or a mother, or a servant, feel for those you care for, and suffer with their sufferings even if they are stubborn and provoke you, and lift up prayers for them, and continue to offer them your love, and do not despair of their repentance and their salvation.

4.17.0.en: Destruction upon destruction: defeat following defeat.

4.17.1.en: My curtains: pieces of cloth set up for dwelling inside them.

4.17.2.en: The prophet continues his suffering because of the series of defeats that will come upon his people, and cries out everywhere about their coming upon them and about the destruction of their dwellings, to which he refers as tents and curtains. What is meant is not only the tents but also the buildings in which they live.

4.18.0.en: Here he makes clear that the Babylonian attack continues for a long time and is repeated against the kingdom of Judah, so that he is no longer able to see the standard of war raised against his people, and the trumpet announcing the continuation of the attack.

4.19.0.en: Here he affirms the reason for this ruin, which is the ignorance and foolishness of the people of God, who departed from His worship and from taking refuge in Him. Although they are the children of God, they did not realize the importance of sonship, and did not live by it in obedience to their Father. On the contrary, they directed their minds and abilities to doing sin instead of worshiping God and doing good.

4.20.0.en: The prophet shows the results of the Babylonian attack on the kingdom of Judah, and declares the devastation of the land, the emigration of people from the ruined cities, and the disappearance of the inhabitants, with the burning of cities rising to heaven, so that the heavens no longer gave their light through the sun and the moon.

4.21.0.en: The people of God worshiped the pagan gods on the mountains and hills, which they thought a symbol of strength because of their height, but now they are worthless before the Babylonian attack, and the pagan gods were not able to protect them, and their weakness is expressed by the shaking and trembling of these high places.

4.21.1.en: The earth signifies the people, and the heavens the priests and pastors, while the mountains and hills signify the leaders, that is, all became humiliated before this ruin because of their sins and their distance from God.

4.22.0.en: The Jews fled in fear for their lives from the face of the Babylonians, and even the birds of the heavens could not remain because of the fires and the noise and all the disturbance of war, so there was no longer rest or safety for anyone, neither for man nor for beast.

4.23.0.en: The orchards and fields and all the cultivated lands turned into ruin and became like the barren desert. All this ruin was by God's permission, using the power of the Babylonians in it, to declare His wrath against His people so that they repent and return to Him.

4.23.1.en: It is noted that he said the word “I beheld” four times in the four preceding verses, as if he were calling out in the four directions of the world, warning all the people, so that they repent, because of the ruin coming upon them.

4.24.0.en: The love of God appears, who allows ruin, but not complete ruin; He leaves a remnant, because He does not intend their destruction but their repentance.

4.25.0.en: God declares His determination to discipline His people; He does everything so that they repent when they enter into this distress and weeping over what they have come to, so that they lose their confidence in the pagan gods and return to God.

4.26.0.en: He declares the signs of the ruin brought about by the Babylonian attack with its horsemen, the archers. The signs of this ruin are the flight of all, the destruction of the cities, and people's taking refuge in the forests and mountains and sheltering behind the rocks so that they would not die.

4.27.0.en: Crimson: garments of a dark red color worn by kings and the great.

4.27.1.en: Antimony: the kohl that is put around the eyes.

4.27.2.en: God addresses the kingdom of Judah, which will be destroyed by the Babylonians, and warns her against relying on her own strength, that is, self-righteousness. He compares her to a woman who wears costly crimson garments and adorns herself with gold and silver, and puts cosmetics on her face, such as kohl, to show her beauty, and He says to her that all this will not profit you and the Babylonians will ruin you. By this He points to the necessity that His people not rely on the outward forms of worship, and the presence of the temple among them in Jerusalem, or on their strength, or their strange gods, for all this is worthless before the wrath of God, and the only solution is repentance with humility.

4.28.0.en: Travailing: the woman who gives birth and is in pain with the pangs of childbirth.

4.28.1.en: The anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child: the woman in her first childbirth suffers more pains than one who has given birth more than once. Sigh: breathes out the air from her nose and mouth with a clear sound, a sign of severe pain.

4.28.2.en: He goes on with his comparisons to show the sufferings of his people, and compares the kingdom of Judah to a woman giving birth and in pain with the pangs of childbirth; indeed, he declares that her pains are severe like the pains of one giving birth for the first time, and the sound of her sighing declares her agonies, and from the abundance of suffering and grief she throws herself on the ground, spreading out her arms and hands, and loses consciousness because of all that she sees of the ferocity of the Babylonian attack.

4.28.3.en: Humble yourself in repentance for all your sins, and you will save your soul by the mercies of God from many afflictions and obtain an unspeakable peace.

4.28.4.en: God's discipline of Jerusalem so that she repents
